reuse.why: Builds on the tree's WeekendRule/applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay abstraction and RSchedule, adding a shared isNonWorkingDay and skipsWeekendOccurrences predicate instead of new ad hoc checks.

duplication.why: The 'skip this occurrence if daily and non-working' filter (skipsWeekendOccurrences + isNonWorkingDay, plus a widened take/margin) is re-expressed at four call sites rather than provided by one occurrence-selection helper.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday predicates live in shared/schedules.ts next to the existing rule; only the occurrence filtering and look-ahead padding leak into server handlers and the budget template.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps with tests and release notes; the import reorder in app.ts is trivial noise.

maintainability.why: Named predicates make the rule readable, but the skip decision and the over-fetch heuristics (14, count*7, margin) are spread across four places with slightly different WeekendRule shapes passed at each.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange and getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (budget/schedule-template.ts) apply the daily-skip filter themselves around applyWeekendRule; getUpcomingDates also builds its WeekendRule without frequency

disguised_duplication.where: the skip filter appears as isKept in getNextDate, a continue in getDatesInRange's loop, a .filter in getUpcomingDates and a guarded monthlyTarget increment in schedule-template.ts

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays, getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; applyWeekendRule and applyWeekendRuleToDay gain a !skipsWeekendOccurrences branch; getDatesInRange, getUpcomingDates and schedule-template re-implement the skip filter
